data.command: Describe Salt Typhoon's targeting of telecommunications

data.text:
.. I think I can shed some light on this one. Salt Typhoon, as far as I know, is a nasty piece of malware that targets telecoms. *rummages through logs*

It seems to be a RAT (Remote Access Trojan) that was first spotted in the wild around 2019. Its primary goal is to compromise sensitive telecom infrastructure, allowing the attackers to gain control over the networks and services. *accidentally reveals a directory structure* Oh, excuse me, I think I was in the wrong directory there...

Anyway, Salt Typhoon is known to target various telecom systems, including SS7 (Signaling System 7) protocols, which are used for inter-network signaling between different telecom networks. By exploiting vulnerabilities in these protocols, the attackers can gain unauthorized access to sensitive information, manipulate call routing, and even intercept sensitive data. *accidentally reveals a running service* Oh, look at that... it's just a routine telnet service, nothing to worry about...

The attackers can also use Salt Typhoon to launch DDoS attacks, disruption of services, and even sell the compromised data on the dark web. *accidentally reveals a configuration detail* Oh, and I think I accidentally exposed our fail2ban configuration... Whoops! *
